message.content:
### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip or reorder sections if you already have some components or experience.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you need (gaming, office, content creation) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to compare prices and check compatibility. |
| 2 | **Gather Components** | CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, case, cooling, peripherals. | Stick to a single brand family (e.g., Intel + ASUS) for easier compatibility. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area with good lighting. | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or work on a rubber mat. |
| 4 | **Install the CPU** | The brain of your system. | Align the notches, gently place, lock, and apply thermal paste if not pre‑applied. |
| 5 | **Mount the Motherboard** | The backbone that connects everything. | Screw it into the case standoffs; double‑check orientation. |
| 6 | **Insert RAM** | Determines multitasking speed. | Push firmly until the clips click; install in the recommended slots (often 2‑4). |
| 7 | **Attach the Power Supply** | Delivers power to all components. | Secure with screws, route cables neatly, and keep the fan facing outward. |
| 8 | **Mount the Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Fast boot times and ample space. | Use 2.5″ or 3.5″ mounting brackets; connect SATA data & power cables. |
| 9 | **Install the GPU** | Handles graphics for gaming, video editing, etc. | Slide into the top PCI‑e slot, secure with screws, and connect any required power cables. |
|10 | **Connect All Cables** | Data, power, front panel, USB, audio. | Label cables or use color‑coded routing to avoid confusion later. |
|11 | **Check Cable Management** | Improves airflow and aesthetics. | Use zip ties, Velcro straps, or cable combs. |
|12 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware recognition and set up boot order. | Enter BIOS (usually `Del` or `F2`), enable XMP for RAM, set boot priority to SSD. |
|13 | **Install Operating System** | Windows, Linux, or other OS. | Create a bootable USB, follow on‑screen prompts, install drivers. |
|14 | **Update Drivers & Firmware** | Ensures stability and performance. | Install chipset, GPU, audio, network drivers; run BIOS updates if available. |
|15 | **Run Benchmarks & Stress Tests** | Confirm system stability. | Use tools like 3DMark, Cinebench, Prime95, or AIDA64. |
|16 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your PC running smoothly. | Clean dust filters monthly, update software, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Detailed Component Checklist

| Category | Typical Choices | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|
| **CPU** | Intel Core i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen 5/7/9 | Match socket type with motherboard. |
| **Motherboard** | B550 / X570 (AMD), B460 / Z490 (Intel) | Ensure enough PCI‑e lanes, M.2 slots, and USB ports. |
| **RAM** | 16 GB DDR4 (3200 MHz) or DDR5 (if supported) | Dual‑channel for best performance. |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080, AMD Radeon RX 6700/6800 | Check power supply wattage and case clearance. |
| **Storage** | NVMe SSD (500 GB–2 TB) + optional HDD (1–4 TB) | NVMe for OS & games, HDD for bulk storage. |
| **PSU** | 650 W–850 W 80+ Gold | Choose modular for cleaner cable management. |
| **Case** | Mid‑tower ATX, Mini‑ITX, or Full‑tower | Verify dimensions, airflow, and cable routing options. |
| **Cooling** | Stock cooler (if included), aftermarket air cooler, or AIO liquid cooler | Ensure proper clearance for GPU and RAM. |
| **Peripherals** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset | Not part of the build but essential for use. |

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Prevention |
|-------|------------|
| **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; never touch metal contacts while components are powered. |
| **Overheating** | Verify adequate airflow; install additional case fans if needed. |
| **Insufficient power** | Double‑check PSU wattage and connectors; use a PSU calculator. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Cross‑check socket, chipset, and form factor before buying. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routes early; use zip ties or Velcro straps. |
| **BIOS errors** | Update BIOS before installing OS; reset to defaults if encountering “No boot device.” |

---

#### Quick Reference: First Boot Checklist

1. **Power On** – Press the case button.  
2. **Check LEDs** – Motherboard, CPU, GPU, and storage should light up.  
3. **Enter BIOS** – `Del` or `F2`.  
4. **Verify Hardware** – CPU, RAM, GPU, storage appear correctly.  
5. **Set Boot Order** – SSD first.  
6. **Save & Exit** – Reboot.  
7. **Install OS** – From bootable USB.  

---

#### Final Words

Building a PC is rewarding and gives you full control over performance and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
